body:
## Pull request overview

This PR fixes a critical crash in the `object-chart` component that occurred when non-array data (such as an object) was provided to Recharts, which internally calls `.slice()` expecting an array. The fix implements defensive `Array.isArray()` guards at three layers to ensure only arrays are passed to Recharts.

**Changes:**
- Added defensive Array.isArray checks in ObjectChart, ChartRenderer, and AdvancedChartImpl to convert non-array data to empty arrays
- Updated ROADMAP.md to document the fix

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx | Added Array.isArray guard when resolving final data from boundData/schema.data/fetchedData before passing to ChartRenderer |
| packages/plugin-charts/src/ChartRenderer.tsx | Added Array.isArray guard in useMemo to validate schema.data before constructing props for AdvancedChartImpl |
| packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx | Added defensive Array.isArray guard on the data prop before it reaches Recharts components |
| ROADMAP.md | Documented the fix as a completed task in the plugin-charts section |

The defensive Array.isArray guards added here prevent crashes when non-array data is passed, but there are no tests validating this behavior. Consider adding test cases that verify the component handles non-array data gracefully (e.g., when boundData or schema.data is an object, null, or undefined) and returns an empty array rather than crashing. This would ensure the fix is durable and prevent regressions.

Similar to ObjectChart, this defensive guard should be covered by tests to ensure the component handles non-array schema.data gracefully. Consider adding test cases that verify behavior when schema.data is an object, null, undefined, or other non-array types.

This defensive guard at the implementation layer should have test coverage to verify the component renders correctly when receiving non-array data props, rather than crashing with 'r.slice is not a function'. Consider adding tests that pass invalid data types and verify they're converted to empty arrays.
